newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-INDIA SLIDES, RATE WORRIES HIT TAIWAN.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-INDIA SLIDES, RATE WORRIES HIT TAIWAN.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts were knocked back on Wednesday as the local market fell following a volatile session.
Traders said the market had run into profit-taking after a rumour -- later denied -- that Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gurjal had resigned and on forecasts of weaker cement company earnings.
"We mirrored the fall in the local market but the selling was not as strong as the buying last week," said one London dealer. "The undertone is still firm."
The HSBC James Capel India GDR index was down 1.45 points, or 1.61 percent, at 89.13, a premium of 21.23 percent to the local market. Bombay's benchmark 30-share index shed 25.01 to 4,523.01.
The Cazenove Indian GDR index, which measures changes from midday to midday, fell 1.61 points to 100.32, a premium of 21.30 percent to Bombay.

The Taiwanese GDR market also lost ground as the local market continued its retreat on tightening liquidity. The state-owned Bank of Taiwan, the country's biggest bank, hiked its prime lending rate by 0.125 percentage point to 7.150 percent after the Taipei close.
The Capel Taiwan GDR index was off 1.10, or 0.78 percent, at 140.00, a discount of 1.80 percent to Taipei where the weighted index ended off 58.21 at 9,861.47.
The Capel Korea GDR index added 0.27 points, or 0.35 percent, to 76.70, a premium of 46.37 percent to the local market.
